items.markdown:
Thailand's weather features three main seasons—`cool-dry, hot, and rainy` —varying by high-season comfort, peak heat, and monsoon downpours.[](https://www.tui.co.uk/holidays/weather/asia/thailand.html) [[1]](https://www.tui.co.uk/holidays/weather/asia/thailand.html)[[2]](https://www.tourismthailand.org/Plan-Your-Trip/Weather?province=219)[[3]](https://www.weather2travel.com/thailand/climate/)[[4]](https://northabroad.com/when-to-visit-thailand/)[[5]](https://www.bambootravel.co.uk/holidays-to-thailand/when-to-visit)

Cool and Dry Season (November to February)

- **November** : Transition into the cooler dry period; pleasant temperatures and lower humidity.
- **December** : The coolest month nationally, averaging 26°C (79°F) with abundant sunshine.
- **January** : Peak travel month, very dry, clear skies, and comfortable temperatures (24°C–32°C).
- **February** : Warm, dry, and sunny, with great beach and island conditions.[](https://www.tui.co.uk/holidays/weather/asia/thailand.html) [[1]](https://www.holiday-weather.com/bangkok/averages/)[[2]](https://www.enchantingtravels.com/destinations/asia/thailand/best-time-to-visit-thailand/)[[3]](https://www.tourradar.com/tg/weather-in-thailand)[[4]](https://www.kuoni.co.uk/destinations/asia/south-east-asia/thailand/best-time-to-visit/)

Hot Season (March to May)

- **March** : Temperatures rise sharply, reaching average highs of 35°C (95°F) with minimal rain.
- **April** : The hottest month of the year, with inland and Bangkok temperatures soaring past 40°C (104°F) and the Songkran festival.
- **May** : Transition month as the southwest monsoon begins; high heat continues alongside increasing afternoon showers.[](https://www.gadventures.com/blog/thailand-weather/) [[1]](https://www.gadventures.com/blog/thailand-weather/)

Rainy / Monsoon Season (June to October)

- **June & July** : Frequent rain showers and high humidity, though often arriving as heavy, short-lived afternoon downpours.
- **August** : Wetter monsoon conditions expand across most of the country, keeping landscapes lush.
- **September** : Statistically the wettest month of the year in central and upper Thailand, averaging over 220–250mm of rain.
- **October** : Heavy rains begin to ease in most regions, though southern areas (like the Gulf coast) can experience delayed wet weather patterns.[](https://www.gadventures.com/blog/thailand-weather/) [[1]](https://www.thomascook.com/holidays/weather/thailand/)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H2VaUUisNgE&t=44)[[3]](https://www.experiencetravelgroup.com/inspiration/seasonal-guides/when-to-go-to-thailand)

If you have a specific destination in mind—such as **Bangkok, Phuket, or Koh Samui** —or a **target month** for your trip, let me know and I can give you localized regional advice!
